import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def kmpSearch_precond (haystack : Array UInt8) (needle : Array UInt8) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  haystack.size < 1000000 ∧ 
  needle.size < 1000000
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
/-- Boolean test that a pattern matches at a given position. -/
def byteMatchesAtB (haystack needle : Array UInt8) (i : Nat) : Bool :=
  decide (i + needle.size ≤ haystack.size) &&
    (List.range needle.size).all fun j =>
      haystack.getD (i + j) 0 == needle.getD j 0

/-- Boolean test that `k` is a proper border of a prefix of length `len`. -/
def isProperBorderB (needle : Array UInt8) (len k : Nat) : Bool :=
  decide (k < len) &&
    (List.range k).all fun j =>
      needle.getD j 0 == needle.getD (len - k + j) 0

/-- Greatest proper-border length of the prefix ending at `i`. -/
def lpsAt (needle : Array UInt8) (i : Nat) : Nat :=
  Nat.findGreatest
    (fun k => isProperBorderB needle (i + 1) k = true) i

/-- Longest-prefix-suffix table for the pattern. -/
def computeLPS (needle : Array UInt8) : Array Nat :=
  Array.ofFn fun i : Fin needle.size => lpsAt needle i.val
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def kmpSearch (haystack : Array UInt8) (needle : Array UInt8)
    (_ : kmpSearch_precond haystack needle) : Array Nat :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  ((List.range (haystack.size + 1)).filter
    (fun i => byteMatchesAtB haystack needle i)).toArray
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition auxiliary definitions
def matchesAt (haystack needle : Array UInt8) (i : Nat) : Prop :=
  i + needle.size ≤ haystack.size ∧
  (∀ j, j < needle.size → haystack.getD (i + j) 0 = needle.getD j 0)

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def kmpSearch_postcond (haystack : Array UInt8) (needle : Array UInt8)
    (result : Array Nat) (_ : kmpSearch_precond haystack needle) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  (∀ i, i < result.size → matchesAt haystack needle (result.getD i 0)) ∧ -- Soundness
  (∀ i, matchesAt haystack needle i → ∃ k, k < result.size ∧ result.getD k 0 = i) -- Completeness
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
lemma byteMatchesAtB_iff_matchesAt
    (haystack needle : Array UInt8) (i : Nat) :
    byteMatchesAtB haystack needle i = true ↔
      matchesAt haystack needle i := by
  simp [byteMatchesAtB, matchesAt, List.all_eq_true]

lemma list_exists_getElem_of_mem {α : Type*} (a : α) (xs : List α)
    (h : a ∈ xs) :
    ∃ (k : Nat) (hk : k < xs.length), xs[k] = a := by
  induction xs with
  | nil =>
      simp at h
  | cons b xs ih =>
      simp only [List.mem_cons] at h
      rcases h with h | h
      · subst b
        exact ⟨0, by simp, by simp⟩
      · obtain ⟨k, hk, heq⟩ := ih h
        refine ⟨k + 1, ?_, ?_⟩
        · simp only [List.length_cons]
          omega
        · simpa using heq

lemma getD_toArray_eq_getElem {α : Type*} (xs : List α) (k : Nat)
    (fallback : α) (hk : k < xs.length) :
    xs.toArray.getD k fallback = xs[k] := by
  simp [Array.getD, hk]
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem kmpSearch_postcond_satisfied (haystack : Array UInt8) (needle : Array UInt8)
    (h_precond : kmpSearch_precond haystack needle) :
    kmpSearch_postcond haystack needle (kmpSearch haystack needle h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  let xs :=
    (List.range (haystack.size + 1)).filter
      (fun i => byteMatchesAtB haystack needle i)

  constructor
  · intro i hi

    have hi' : i < xs.length := by
      simpa [kmpSearch, xs] using hi

    have hmem : xs[i] ∈ xs :=
      List.getElem_mem hi'

    have hbool :
        byteMatchesAtB haystack needle xs[i] = true :=
      (List.mem_filter.mp hmem).2

    have hmatch : matchesAt haystack needle xs[i] :=
      (byteMatchesAtB_iff_matchesAt haystack needle xs[i]).mp hbool

    have hget :
        xs.toArray.getD i 0 = xs[i] :=
      getD_toArray_eq_getElem xs i 0 hi'

    change matchesAt haystack needle (xs.toArray.getD i 0)
    rw [hget]
    exact hmatch

  · intro i hmatch

    have hi_le : i ≤ haystack.size := by
      have hi_add : i ≤ i + needle.size :=
        Nat.le_add_right i needle.size
      exact hi_add.trans hmatch.1

    have hrange : i ∈ List.range (haystack.size + 1) := by
      simp
      omega

    have hbool : byteMatchesAtB haystack needle i = true :=
      (byteMatchesAtB_iff_matchesAt haystack needle i).mpr hmatch

    have hmem : i ∈ xs := by
      apply List.mem_filter.mpr
      exact ⟨hrange, hbool⟩

    obtain ⟨k, hk, hget⟩ :=
      list_exists_getElem_of_mem i xs hmem

    refine ⟨k, ?_, ?_⟩
    · simpa [kmpSearch, xs] using hk
    · have hgetD :
          xs.toArray.getD k 0 = xs[k] :=
        getD_toArray_eq_getElem xs k 0 hk
      change xs.toArray.getD k 0 = i
      exact hgetD.trans hget
  -- !benchmark @end proof

Natural language description:
Your task is to implement the Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP) algorithm to efficiently find all occurrences of a needle (pattern) within a haystack (text) and verify its functional correctness in Lean using Mathlib. Preconditions: You can assume the input text and pattern are arrays of UInt8 (representing bytes) and their lengths are at most 1,000,000. Requirements: Implement the method kmpSearch which returns an Array Nat. (1) Preprocessing: You must implement a helper to compute the Longest Prefix Suffix (LPS) array (or "next" array), where lps[i] stores the length of the longest proper prefix of the sub-pattern that is also a suffix of that sub-pattern. (2) Search: The main loop must use the LPS array to skip unnecessary comparisons in the text when a mismatch occurs, achieving linear time complexity. (3) Functional Correctness: Prove that despite the optimization, the result is identical to a naive search (Soundness and Completeness). Verification Challenges: (1) LPS Property: Proving that your preprocessing logic actually satisfies the mathematical definition of the LPS table. (2) Safe Skipping: Proving that the "jump" logic (moving the pattern index based on LPS) never skips a valid match. (3) Complex Invariants: The main loop invariant must relate the current state of the pattern index to the prefix of the pattern matched against the text so far.
